title: RMOS-CONVERGE-001B: make former draft retract paths an explicit governed contract
intent: Stacked follow-up to RMOS-CONVERGE-001B (#314), superseding the #315 draft as the thing to merge into #314. The checkpoint PR converged all four retract G-code routes onto one authority boundary but left the draft-to-governed header/path contract implicit, which would silently break consumers that still treated /gcode and /gcode/download as draft-lane 200 G-code. This patch documents that contract, advertises X-ToolBox-Lane: governed and X-Run-ID on 409, locks it with witnesses, retires the smoke-test restore-to-draft assertions, stops the in-tree Vue exporter from downloading 409 JSON as a .nc file, and proves POST /gcode binds query params (a JSON body is ignored) with OpenAPI/HTTP/builder guards plus Vue tests for readGcodeOrThrow and exportGcode.
behavior_change: INTENTIONAL compatibility contract. Former draft retract URLs already returned 409 SAFETY_BLOCKED under #314; they now also send X-ToolBox-Lane: governed and X-Run-ID on that 409 (and still will after an evaluator lands — they will not revert to draft). The Vue retract exporter no longer treats a non-OK body as G-code; it surfaces SAFETY_BLOCKED instead of saving JSON as .nc. Query params are now sent (the previous JSON body was ignored by FastAPI).

diff_articulation.what_changed: (1) retract_gcode_router.py: 409 SAFETY_BLOCKED now carries X-ToolBox-Lane: governed and X-Run-ID via a shared header helper; module and endpoint docs state that /gcode and /gcode/download are not draft lanes and will not revert to draft when an evaluator lands. Shared Query() objects make /gcode and /gcode_governed query-string bound in OpenAPI so they cannot be confused with /gcode/download (JSON body). (2) Census adds an explicit before/after/after-evaluator contract table and names the Vue consumer. (3) Convergence tests assert governed headers on 409, drop the brittle source-index order check for AST/call-graph invariants, and split the literal-RunDecision guard so it is named as forbidding any hardcoded risk_level. (4) Smoke tests that encoded restore-to-draft are rewritten to the governed contract; the letter-G false positive is replaced with machine-marker checks. (5) useRetractOperation sends query params and refuses to download non-OK bodies; useGcodeExport adds readGcodeOrThrow. (6) Rebased onto #314's fence resolution (validate_and_persist persistence, risk_level carried forward from the authorization, explicit retract mode constants) and, on owner direction, restored a STRUCTURAL authorization-before-generation invariant: test_authorization_structurally_precedes_generation asserts order and dependency on the AST - unconditional top-level gate, _build_* at a strictly later statement index, persisted artifact carrying run_id and risk_level from the authorizing call, and an HTTPException raise guarded by SafetyPolicy.should_block. Statement index, not source offset, so comments and renamed locals cannot break it; verified by three mutations. This is the only witness that survives the lane reopening - the 409 witnesses prove today's no-evaluator state only. (7) The generalized alert-detail change to handleExportError is withdrawn: it altered behaviour for five unrelated CAM operations. Detail is now opt-in via a showDetail flag that only the retract caller passes. (8) The 20 verbatim xfail reason blocks are hoisted to one module-level `blocked_by_design` marker. (9) The convergence fixture's local `store._default_store = None` is removed - store.py re-exports that name as an import-time value binding, so the assignment never touched the singleton the endpoints read, and the session conftest already resets the real one. (10) Query-binding proof: OpenAPI declares /gcode scalars as query not body; an HTTP test shows query values reach request_summary/tool_id and a JSON body is ignored; the builder embeds those scalars. Vue tests cover readGcodeOrThrow (200 text, 409 SAFETY_BLOCKED, non-JSON error) and exportGcode query-string POST without downloadFile on 409. (11) docs/api/endpoints.md states consumer impact plainly: clients that keyed on draft or assumed all 200/POST export bodies were G-code must change.
diff_articulation.why_not_redundant: The #314 checkpoint changed live production endpoints from draft 200 G-code to governed 409 without making the header/path contract observable or updating the in-tree consumer. That is the blocking review concern: old paths plus new behaviour silently breaks callers. This patch is that contract, not a second census or a new evaluator. The query-binding tests close the remaining #315 merge-readiness gap: proving the Vue query-string POST matches FastAPI, rather than silently changing a JSON-body contract that never existed.
